text:
Mathieu Joseph won two Stanley Cups in Tampa Bay and has made a career out of being the useful depth forward contenders like to have. In Edmonton this season the scoring has been fine, eight points in 18 games, but the five-on-five results have not: the Oilers have taken just 37% of the expected goals with him on the ice, about 15 points worse than without him. Sportskeeda put him on its list of disappointing Oilers after the 5-4 loss to Anaheim.

The points are partly a mirage. He has three goals on 1.7 expected, a 20% shooting percentage, and his minutes have dropped by more than two a night over his last ten games.

His game has always lived elsewhere. Evolving-Hockey had his value last season coming from defense, with opponents getting fewer chances against him than against 86% of forwards, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows 73% of his exits leaving with possession and three-quarters of his shots coming off the rush. Our range says 6 to 14 goals over a full season. Edmonton needs the old defensive version back.
headline: Joseph needs his old game back
